<ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
<TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
<EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>true</EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>
<Company>Contoso</Company>
<Authors>Contoso Engineering</Authors>
```

That's **7 properties × 5 files = 35 lines** of pure duplication. When you need to change the target framework to `net9.0`, you must edit all 5 files. This is the textbook case for a **`Directory.Build.props`** at the repo root.

**Recommended `Directory.Build.props`** (repo root):

```xml
<Project>
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
    <EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>true</EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>
    <Company>Contoso</Company>
    <Authors>Contoso Engineering</Authors>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

Then remove all 7 properties from every `.csproj`.

### 2. Duplicated `DocumentationFile` property in all 3 src projects

All three src projects contain:

```xml
<DocumentationFile>$(OutputPath)$(AssemblyName).xml</DocumentationFile>
```

This should also move into `Directory.Build.props` — but scoped to src projects only, since test projects don't set it. Two clean approaches:

**Option A** — Condition on `IsPackable` (test projects already set `<IsPackable>false</IsPackable>`):

```xml
<!-- In root Directory.Build.props -->
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(IsPackable)' != 'false'">
  <DocumentationFile>$(OutputPath)$(AssemblyName).xml</DocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Option B** — A second `Directory.Build.props` in the `src/` folder:

```xml
<!-- src/Directory.Build.props -->
<Import Project="$([MSBuild]::GetPathOfFileAbove('Directory.Build.props', '$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)../'))" />
<Project>
  <PropertyGroup>
    <DocumentationFile>$(OutputPath)$(AssemblyName).xml</DocumentationFile>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

> **Note:** When using a multi-level `Directory.Build.props` hierarchy, the inner file must **explicitly import** the outer one via `GetPathOfFileAbove`, because MSBuild only auto-imports the nearest one.

### 3. Duplicated `PrintBuildInfo` custom target in all 3 src projects

All three src projects define an identical target:

```xml
<Target Name="PrintBuildInfo" BeforeTargets="Build">
  <Message Importance="high" Text="Building $(AssemblyName) [$(Configuration)]" />
</Target>
```

This target should be defined **once** in a `Directory.Build.targets` file (either at the repo root if you want it for all projects, or in `src/` if only for src projects):

**Recommended `src/Directory.Build.targets`** (or repo-root):

```xml
<Project>
  <Target Name="PrintBuildInfo" BeforeTargets="Build">
    <Message Importance="high" Text="Building $(AssemblyName) [$(Configuration)]" />
  </Target>
</Project>
```

> Targets go in `.targets`, not `.props`, because they must be evaluated after all properties are defined. This is a common mistake — see the `directory-build-organization` skill for the evaluation order: `.props` → SDK `.props` → `.csproj` → SDK `.targets` → `.targets`.

### 4. Test package version drift between the two test projects

| Package | `Core.Tests` | `Api.Tests` |
|---|---|---|
| `Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk` | **17.10.0** | **17.9.0** |
| `xunit` | **2.8.1** | **2.7.1** |
| `xunit.runner.visualstudio` | **2.8.1** | **2.5.6** |
| `NSubstitute` | 5.1.0 | 5.1.0 |

Three out of four test packages are at different versions. This means:
- Tests may behave differently between the two projects.
- A passing test in `Core.Tests` could fail in `Api.Tests` due to test-infrastructure differences.
- Updating packages requires touching multiple files.

**Fix:** Align versions and adopt Central Package Management (see Suggestion §3).

### 5. Multiple `<PropertyGroup>` blocks in src projects

Each src project splits properties across two `<PropertyGroup>` blocks — one for common settings and one for `DocumentationFile`. While not incorrect, it hurts readability. If `DocumentationFile` stays in the `.csproj` (rather than moving to `Directory.Build.props`), consolidate into one `<PropertyGroup>`.

---

## 🔵 Suggestions

### 1. Adopt Central Package Management (CPM)

With 5 projects and already-visible version drift, this repo is an ideal candidate for CPM. Create:

**`Directory.Packages.props`** (repo root):

```xml
<Project>
  <PropertyGroup>
    <ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>true</ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <ItemGroup>
    <!-- Shared -->
    <PackageVersion Include="Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions" Version="8.0.1" />
    <PackageVersion Include="System.Text.Json" Version="8.0.5" />
    <PackageVersion Include="Newtonsoft.Json" Version="13.0.3" />
    <PackageVersion Include="Swashbuckle.AspNetCore" Version="6.5.0" />
    <!-- Test -->
    <PackageVersion Include="Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk" Version="17.10.0" />
    <PackageVersion Include="xunit" Version="2.8.1" />
    <PackageVersion Include="xunit.runner.visualstudio" Version="2.8.1" />
    <PackageVersion Include="NSubstitute" Version="5.1.0" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```

Then in every `.csproj`, drop the `Version` attribute:

```xml
<PackageReference Include="xunit" />   <!-- version managed centrally -->
```

This eliminates all version duplication and makes future upgrades a single-file change.

### 2. Consider adding `<GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>` instead

Rather than manually constructing the `DocumentationFile` path:

```xml
<!-- Current (manual) -->
<DocumentationFile>$(OutputPath)$(AssemblyName).xml</DocumentationFile>
```

The modern SDK property is simpler:

```xml
<!-- Modern -->
<GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
```

This sets `DocumentationFile` automatically with the correct path. Less to maintain, fewer edge cases.

### 3. Add `<IsPackable>false</IsPackable>` for test projects via a `test/Directory.Build.props`

Both test projects set `<IsPackable>false</IsPackable>`. If more test projects are added later, this should be centralized:

```xml
<!-- test/Directory.Build.props -->
<Import Project="$([MSBuild]::GetPathOfFileAbove('Directory.Build.props', '$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)../'))" />
<Project>
  <PropertyGroup>
    <IsPackable>false</IsPackable>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

### 4. Redundant `System.Text.Json` in `ContosoApp.Api`

`ContosoApp.Api` directly references `System.Text.Json` **and** references `ContosoApp.Core` which also references `System.Text.Json`. The transitive reference from `Core` is sufficient for the `Api` project. The explicit reference in `Api` is redundant unless `Api` needs to pin a specific version. If it's unintentional, remove it to reduce maintenance surface.

---

## 🟢 Positives

1. **SDK-style projects throughout** — No legacy `<Import Project="$(MSBuildToolsPath)...">` or `ToolsVersion` attributes. All 5 projects use the modern SDK format. No modernization migration needed.

2. **`TreatWarningsAsErrors` enabled everywhere** — Good build hygiene. Prevents warning accumulation.

3. **`EnforceCodeStyleInBuild` enabled** — Code style rules run during build, not just in IDE. Ensures CI catches style violations.

4. **`Nullable` reference types enabled** — Modern null-safety is active across all projects.

---

## Recommended End State

After applying all recommendations, here's what the file layout and trimmed projects would look like:

```
/
├── Directory.Build.props          ← common properties (7 props)
├── Directory.Build.targets        ← PrintBuildInfo target
├── Directory.Packages.props       ← all package versions (CPM)
├── src/
│   ├── Directory.Build.props      ← GenerateDocumentationFile (imports parent)
│   ├── ContosoApp.Core/
│   │   └── ContosoApp.Core.csproj             ← ~8 lines
│   ├── ContosoApp.Services/
│   │   └── ContosoApp.Services.csproj         ← ~10 lines
│   └── ContosoApp.Api/
│       └── ContosoApp.Api.csproj              ← ~12 lines
└── test/
    ├── Directory.Build.props      ← IsPackable=false (imports parent)
    ├── ContosoApp.Core.Tests/
    │   └── ContosoApp.Core.Tests.csproj       ← ~10 lines
    └── ContosoApp.Api.Tests/
        └── ContosoApp.Api.Tests.csproj        ← ~10 lines
```

**Example trimmed `ContosoApp.Core.csproj`:**

```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions" />
    <PackageReference Include="System.Text.Json" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```

Down from 22 lines to 6. Multiply across 5 projects and you eliminate ~80 lines of duplicated XML while gaining single-point-of-change for framework version, package versions, and shared build behavior.
